newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end pit trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end pit trading mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended pit trading mixed after most units spent another session floating inside tight intraday ranges.
Yen sagged most late and hit session lows into the close on scattered chart-based sales, floor brokers said, while the mark and Canadian dollar returned toward their price troughs.
Brokers said they saw no big futures order flows behind the yen's late renewed erosion, which some instead pinned to technicals as the unit negated Monday's bullish behavior.
"They turned around the bullish signal from Monday," said one broker. "That's a real fresh signal."
Canadian finance minister Paul Martin gives his autumn update on Canada's budget deficit on Wednesday, and Canadian employment figures for August are due on Friday.

The Swiss franc before midday hit its low, a move that coincided with news that Swiss National Bank board member Bruno Gehrig told a Swiss newspaper the SNB expects the Swiss franc to weaken slightly as effects of its recent discount rate cut are not yet fully reflected in exchange rate.
But some said that nearby unit also was snagged inside a range and needs to rise above about $0.8080 or fall below roughly $0.8005 to rouse fresh interest.
"We've been from $0.8077 down to $0.8020 a bunch of times. So there's not really a lot of paper," said another floor broker. "So anything below $0.8005 or above $0.8080, it's going to be busy."
Swiss francs and marks rose early after comments on Monday and Tuesday by Bundesbank officials that suggested little room for easing in EMU convergence criteria.
Comments by various U.S. Federal Reserve Bank presidents on Tuesday had little effect on currencies.
Richmond Fed's Alfred Broaddus said he said some tentative signs the U.S. economy was slowing into the third quarter.
